tareas.titulo_es: Por qué a los jóvenes les cuesta encontrar un empleo estable
tareas.enunciado: Your local newspaper is collecting readers' opinions on youth unemployment. Write a short opinion article explaining why it is difficult for young people in your country to find a stable job and suggest two measures that could help. Give your article a title.
estructura: Título breve y una frase inicial que presente el problema
Primera causa, con una consecuencia concreta
Segunda causa
Dos medidas concretas, introducidas con conectores (on the one hand / on the other hand)
Conclusión breve con tu opinión
expresiones: One of the main reasons is…
It would be a good idea to…
tareas.modelo:
Young people deserve a fair start

Finding a stable job is one of the biggest worries for young people in Spain today. In my opinion, there are two main reasons for this situation.

First, many companies offer only temporary contracts to new workers. As a result, young people move from one short job to another and cannot plan their future, rent a flat or start a family.

Second, there is often a gap between what students learn and what employers need. Many graduates have good theoretical knowledge but little practical experience.

So what could be done? On the one hand, the government could give tax advantages to firms that turn temporary contracts into permanent ones. On the other hand, universities and vocational schools should work more closely with businesses, for instance by offering paid internships.

To sum up, youth unemployment is not inevitable. With better contracts and better training, young people could finally build their lives with confidence.

tareas.titulo_es: ¿Quién paga el precio de la inflación?
tareas.enunciado: An economics magazine has invited its readers to answer the question «Who pays the price of inflation?». Write an opinion article explaining which groups are most affected by rising prices and what governments and central banks should do about it. Give your article a title.
estructura: Título y entrada: la inflación como «impuesto oculto» que no afecta a todos por igual
Quién pierde más (hogares de renta baja, pensionistas, salarios no indexados) y por qué
Quién puede salir ganando (deudores a tipo fijo), para matizar
Qué deben hacer el banco central y el gobierno (subida de tipos, ayudas focalizadas frente a generales)
Conclusión: la estabilidad de precios como cuestión de equidad
expresiones: Inflation is often described as a hidden tax
to bring inflation back to target
tareas.modelo:
Who really pays the price of inflation?

Inflation is often described as a hidden tax, and like many taxes, it does not fall equally on everyone. When prices rise faster than incomes, it is the most vulnerable households that suffer first.

Low-income families spend a larger share of their budget on essentials such as food, energy and rent. Consequently, a sharp rise in these prices reduces their purchasing power far more than that of wealthier households, who can draw on savings or cut back on non-essential spending. Pensioners and workers whose wages are not regularly updated are in a similar position. By contrast, borrowers with fixed-rate loans may actually benefit, since inflation reduces the real value of their debt.

What, then, should policymakers do? Central banks have a clear mandate: to bring inflation back to target by raising interest rates, even if this slows down the economy for a while. Governments, however, should avoid generalised subsidies that benefit everyone and may even fuel demand. Targeted support for the households most exposed to rising prices is both fairer and cheaper.

In my view, the fight against inflation is not only a technical question but also a matter of fairness. Price stability protects those who have the least, and that is precisely why it deserves to be a priority.

tareas.titulo_es: Por qué los jóvenes no pueden pagar una vivienda
tareas.enunciado: Housing has become unaffordable for many young people in big cities. Write an article for a student website giving your opinion on the causes of the problem and assessing at least two possible solutions (for example, rent controls, building more homes or taxing empty properties). Give your article a title.
estructura: Título y entrada con una pregunta o un dato de la experiencia cotidiana
Causa principal según tu opinión (oferta frente a demanda) y causas secundarias
Valoración de al menos dos soluciones, con ventajas e inconvenientes de cada una
Conclusión: qué priorizarías y por qué
expresiones: The main cause, in my view, is…
supply has not kept up with demand
to tackle the root of the problem
tareas.modelo:
Why can't young people afford a home?

In many large cities, renting a small flat now takes more than half of a young worker's salary, and buying one seems almost impossible. How did we get here?

The main cause, in my view, is simple: supply has not kept up with demand. Jobs and young people are increasingly concentrated in a few big cities, but the number of new homes built there has remained low for years. In addition, the growth of short-term tourist rentals has reduced the number of flats available to residents in some central neighbourhoods.

Several solutions are often proposed. Rent controls are popular because their effects are immediate. However, many economists warn that, in the long run, they may discourage owners from renting and reduce the quality of the housing stock. Building more homes, especially social housing, is a slower solution, but it tackles the root of the problem. Taxing empty properties could also help to bring unused flats back onto the market.

All things considered, I believe the priority should be to increase supply, by releasing land and speeding up planning permission, while protecting the most vulnerable tenants in the meantime. Without more homes, any other measure will only bring temporary relief.

tareas.titulo_es: El turismo de masas: ¿bendición o maldición?
tareas.enunciado: «Mass tourism does more harm than good.» Write an opinion essay for an online magazine discussing this statement. Present arguments for and against and give your own view. Give your essay a title.
estructura: Título y entrada: importancia del turismo y protestas recientes de los residentes
Argumentos en contra del turismo de masas (vivienda, comercio local, servicios públicos, empleo estacional)
Argumentos a favor (empleo, pymes, despoblación, patrimonio)
Tu opinión: el problema es la gestión, con dos o tres propuestas
Frase final que cierre el razonamiento
expresiones: On the other hand, it would be unfair to ignore…
In my opinion, the problem is not… but…
tareas.modelo:
Mass tourism: a blessing or a curse?

Tourism is one of the pillars of the Spanish economy. It creates jobs, brings in foreign currency and has helped many regions to develop. Yet in recent years, more and more residents of popular destinations have protested against what they see as an invasion.

Those who criticise mass tourism point to several problems. Housing in city centres becomes more expensive as flats are turned into holiday rentals. Local shops are replaced by souvenir stores, and public services, from transport to water supply, come under pressure during the peak season. Moreover, many tourism jobs are seasonal and poorly paid.

On the other hand, it would be unfair to ignore the benefits. Tourism supports thousands of small businesses, from restaurants to family hotels, and it often keeps alive areas that would otherwise lose their population. It also helps to finance the protection of monuments and natural sites.

In my opinion, the problem is not tourism itself but the way it is managed. Destinations should spread visitors throughout the year, regulate holiday rentals and invest part of the income from tourism in local services. Well managed, tourism can benefit both visitors and residents.

tareas.titulo_es: ¿Puede justificarse el proteccionismo?
tareas.enunciado: Following a new wave of tariff increases between major economies, a business newspaper asks its readers: «Can protectionism ever be justified?». Write an opinion article presenting your position. Take into account the economic arguments on both sides and the implications for a medium-sized open economy such as Spain.
estructura: Título y entrada: vuelta de los aranceles y planteamiento de la pregunta
Argumentos a favor de cierta protección (industria naciente, seguridad de suministro, costes concentrados de la apertura)
Argumentos en contra (incidencia en consumidores y empresas, represalias, cadenas de valor)
Aplicación al caso de una economía abierta como España y papel de la UE
Conclusión: instrumentos alternativos y focalizados
expresiones: The case for protection is not entirely without merit
tareas.modelo:
Protectionism: a tempting but costly remedy

Tariffs are back in fashion. After decades of trade liberalisation, governments in several major economies are once again using them to protect domestic industries, put pressure on rivals or secure supply chains. The question is whether this shift is justified.

The case for protection is not entirely without merit. Economists have long acknowledged that temporary support may help infant industries to reach a competitive scale, and recent crises have shown the dangers of depending on a single supplier for critical goods such as medicines or semiconductors. Furthermore, the costs of trade opening have been concentrated in specific regions, whose discontent cannot simply be dismissed.

Nevertheless, the evidence suggests that tariffs are a blunt and expensive instrument. They are paid largely by domestic consumers and firms in the form of higher prices, they invite retaliation and they shelter inefficient producers from the pressure to innovate. In a world of global value chains, a tariff on imported components ultimately penalises a country's own exporters.

For a medium-sized open economy like Spain, a spiral of protectionism would be particularly harmful. Its interest lies in a rules-based trading system and in a strong European Union, which conducts trade policy on behalf of all its members and carries far more weight than any of them could alone.

In short, legitimate concerns about security and fairness are better addressed through targeted instruments, such as diversifying suppliers, using trade defence measures consistent with WTO rules and supporting the workers affected by change, than through across-the-board tariffs.

tareas.titulo_es: Deuda común: ¿un paso hacia una Unión más fuerte?
tareas.enunciado: A European affairs magazine is running a debate on the following question: «Should the EU borrow jointly on a permanent basis to finance shared priorities such as defence, energy and the green transition?». Write an opinion article setting out the arguments on both sides and defending your own position.
estructura: Título y entrada: el precedente del endeudamiento conjunto tras la pandemia
Argumentos a favor (bienes públicos europeos, espacio fiscal, activo seguro en euros)
Argumentos en contra (transferencias permanentes, incentivos a la reforma, rendición de cuentas)
Tu posición: una vía intermedia con condiciones concretas
Cierre con una idea fuerte
expresiones: Supporters of… put forward convincing arguments
There is also a question of…
a middle path is both possible and desirable
tareas.modelo:
Common debt: a step towards a stronger Union?

The joint borrowing launched to finance the recovery after the pandemic broke a long-standing taboo in the European Union. Today, as the Union faces new challenges, from defence to the energy transition, many wonder whether this exceptional instrument should become permanent.

Supporters of common debt put forward convincing arguments. Some priorities, such as cross-border energy networks or a joint defence industry, are European public goods: they benefit all member states, but no single country has sufficient incentive to finance them alone. Borrowing at European level also allows countries with limited fiscal space to invest without jeopardising their own debt sustainability, and it creates a safe asset in euros that could strengthen the international role of the single currency.

Critics, however, raise legitimate concerns. Some member states fear that mutualised debt could turn into a permanent transfer mechanism and weaken the incentive for reform. There is also a question of democratic accountability: who decides how the money is spent, and who will ultimately repay it?

In my opinion, a middle path is both possible and desirable. Common borrowing should be reserved for clearly defined European public goods, linked to measurable objectives and backed by new own resources, so that repayment does not depend on the goodwill of national budgets. Used in this way, it would not be a blank cheque, but a tool for a Union that wishes to act rather than merely react.

Ultimately, the real risk is not borrowing together, but failing to invest together while other major powers do so on a massive scale.

tareas.titulo_es: La transición energética: ¿carga u oportunidad?
tareas.enunciado: An English-language business weekly has asked readers whether the energy transition is an opportunity or a burden for the European economy. Write an opinion article answering this question, with particular reference to a country such as Spain.
estructura: Título y entrada: la percepción de la transición como coste, y tu tesis
Primer argumento: dependencia energética exterior y seguridad de suministro
Segundo argumento: costes de las renovables y ventaja comparativa de España
Concesión: costes de inversión, sectores y regiones perdedores, riesgo de rechazo social
Conclusión: inversión a largo plazo y condiciones para que salga bien
expresiones: It is therefore tempting to see it as…
to turn a natural advantage into…
tareas.modelo:
The energy transition: burden or opportunity?

For many households and firms, the energy transition is associated with costs: more expensive cars, new heating systems, stricter regulations. It is therefore tempting to see it as a burden imposed on the economy for environmental reasons alone. In my view, this perception overlooks the considerable economic opportunities it offers, particularly for countries like Spain.

First of all, Europe imports most of the oil and gas it consumes. The price shock that followed the invasion of Ukraine showed how vulnerable this dependence makes us. Every wind turbine and solar panel installed on European soil reduces that exposure and keeps a larger share of energy spending within the domestic economy.

Secondly, renewables have become one of the cheapest sources of electricity. Countries with abundant sun and wind, such as Spain, could turn this natural advantage into lower costs for industry and attract energy-intensive activities, from green hydrogen to data centres.

That said, the transition will not be painless. It requires massive investment in grids and storage, and some sectors and regions that depend on fossil fuels will lose jobs. If these costs are not shared fairly, public support could quickly erode, as protests in several countries have already shown.

To conclude, the energy transition is neither a free lunch nor an unbearable burden. It is a long-term investment whose returns will depend on sound planning, stable regulation and policies that protect those most exposed to change.

tareas.titulo_es: Inteligencia artificial: ¿productividad o desigualdad?
tareas.enunciado: A quality weekly is publishing a debate on the economic consequences of artificial intelligence. Write an essay assessing whether AI is more likely to raise productivity and living standards or to widen inequalities, and discuss what role public policy should play.
estructura: Título y entrada: previsiones contradictorias y tu tesis matizada
Visión optimista: tecnología de propósito general, ganancias de productividad, efecto en trabajadores menos experimentados
Matices: lecciones de revoluciones tecnológicas anteriores, reparto desigual, concentración del mercado
Papel de la política pública: tres prioridades (formación, competencia, regulación equilibrada)
Conclusión: el resultado depende de las decisiones colectivas
expresiones: Both narratives are overstated, yet each contains a kernel of truth
There is no reason to assume that…
to strike a balance between… and…
will depend less on… than on…
tareas.modelo:
Artificial intelligence: beyond the hype and the fear

Few technologies have generated such contradictory forecasts as artificial intelligence. Some predict a productivity boom that will lift living standards for decades; others foresee mass unemployment and an unprecedented concentration of wealth. Both narratives, in my view, are overstated, yet each contains a kernel of truth.

On the optimistic side, AI has the potential to become what economists call a general-purpose technology, comparable to electricity or the internet. By automating routine cognitive tasks, from drafting documents to analysing data, it could free workers to focus on activities with higher added value. Some early studies even suggest that the largest gains accrue to less experienced employees, which, if confirmed, would narrow rather than widen skill gaps within firms.

History, however, teaches caution. The productivity gains from previous technological revolutions took decades to materialise, because firms had to reorganise their processes and workers had to acquire new skills. In the meantime, the benefits were unevenly shared, and there is no reason to assume that AI will be different. Moreover, the market for the most advanced models is dominated by a handful of companies, mostly outside Europe, which raises legitimate concerns about competition and about who will capture the rents generated by the technology.

Public policy therefore has a decisive role to play, not in slowing down innovation but in shaping its direction. Three priorities stand out. First, education and lifelong learning systems must adapt, so that workers can move into new tasks rather than being displaced. Secondly, competition authorities should ensure that access to data and computing power does not become an insurmountable barrier to entry. Finally, Europe needs to strike a balance between regulation that protects citizens and an environment in which its own firms can grow.

In the final analysis, artificial intelligence is neither a destiny nor a threat in itself. Whether it becomes a source of shared prosperity or of deeper division will depend less on the technology than on the choices societies make in the coming years.

tareas.titulo_es: Carta de reclamación a un banco
tareas.enunciado: You have noticed that your bank has charged you an annual maintenance fee of 60 euros, although when you opened the account you were told that it would be free as long as your salary was paid into it. Write a letter to the customer service department explaining the problem, asking for a refund and saying what you will do if the problem is not solved.
estructura: Saludo formal (Dear Sir or Madam) y motivo de la carta en la primera frase
Explicación de los hechos: lo que te dijeron al abrir la cuenta y lo que ha ocurrido
Petición concreta (devolución) y documentos que adjuntas
Qué harás si no se resuelve (plazo)
Fórmula de cierre (I look forward to… / Yours faithfully) y firma
expresiones: I am writing to complain about…
I believe this charge is a mistake
I would be grateful if you could…
I will have no choice but to…
I look forward to your prompt reply.
tareas.modelo:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a charge on my current account, number ending in 4821.

When I opened the account in March, the bank employee told me clearly that there would be no maintenance fees as long as my salary was paid into it. My salary has been paid into the account every month since then. However, on my latest statement I noticed a fee of 60 euros described as an «annual maintenance charge».

I believe this charge is a mistake, so I would be grateful if you could refund the full amount as soon as possible. I attach a copy of the statement and of the document I signed when I opened the account.

If the problem is not solved within fifteen days, I will have no choice but to file a complaint with the Bank of Spain.

I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,

Laura Martín

tareas.titulo_es: Carta de presentación para unas prácticas en una Oficina Económica y Comercial
tareas.enunciado: You have seen an advertisement for a six-month internship at the Economic and Commercial Office of the Spanish Embassy in London. Write a cover letter presenting your education and experience, explaining why you are interested in the position and what you could contribute to the team.
estructura: Saludo y puesto al que te presentas, con dónde viste el anuncio
Formación y experiencia internacional
Experiencia profesional relevante, con tareas concretas
Motivación y qué aportarías (competencias, idiomas)
Cierre: disponibilidad para una entrevista, CV adjunto y despedida formal
expresiones: I am writing to apply for…
This experience confirmed my interest in…
I am particularly attracted to this position because…
I believe that my… would allow me to…
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application
tareas.modelo:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the six-month internship at the Economic and Commercial Office of the Spanish Embassy in London, as advertised on your website.

I recently graduated in Economics from the University of Valencia, where I specialised in international trade and wrote my final dissertation on the internationalisation of Spanish food companies. During my studies, I also spent a semester at a university in Ireland, which allowed me to improve my English and get used to working in an international environment.

Last summer I worked as an intern in the export department of a family-owned wine company. My tasks included analysing market data, preparing presentations for foreign buyers and helping to organise the company's participation in a trade fair. This experience confirmed my interest in supporting Spanish firms abroad.

I am particularly attracted to this position because it would allow me to see how public institutions help companies to enter new markets. I believe that my analytical skills, my knowledge of the food sector and my ability to communicate in English and French would enable me to make a useful contribution to your team.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application with you. Please find my CV attached.

Yours faithfully,

Javier Ruiz

tareas.titulo_es: Carta al director sobre la despoblación rural
tareas.enunciado: A national newspaper has published a report on depopulation in rural areas, which suggested that the trend is now irreversible. Write a letter to the editor sharing your own experience, explaining why the issue matters for the whole country and proposing measures to reverse the trend.
estructura: Fórmula de apertura de carta al director (Sir, / Dear Editor,) y referencia al artículo
Experiencia personal breve que ilustre el problema
Por qué afecta a todo el país (territorio, incendios, patrimonio, presión sobre las ciudades)
Desacuerdo con una idea del artículo (irreversibilidad) y argumentos
Propuestas y frase final contundente; firma con ciudad
expresiones: Your report on… struck a chord with me
As your article rightly pointed out,
is not merely a local problem
I would, however, take issue with…
tareas.modelo:
Sir,

Your report on rural depopulation, published last Sunday, struck a chord with me. I grew up in a village in the province of Teruel which, when I was a child, had a school, a doctor's surgery and two shops. Today the school has closed, the doctor comes twice a week and the last shop survives thanks to elderly residents who cannot drive to the nearest town.

As your article rightly pointed out, depopulation is not merely a local problem. When villages empty, land is abandoned, forests become more vulnerable to fire and part of our cultural heritage disappears. At the same time, the concentration of the population in a few large cities pushes up housing costs and puts pressure on urban infrastructure. In other words, the whole country pays the price.

I would, however, take issue with the suggestion that the trend is irreversible. The spread of remote working has shown that many professionals would be willing to live in rural areas if they had reliable broadband, decent public services and affordable housing. Some regions have already attracted new residents by combining these elements with tax incentives for young families and businesses.

What is lacking is a long-term strategy rather than isolated initiatives. Investment in digital connectivity, the reorganisation of health and education services on a district basis and support for activities linked to the land, from sustainable farming to rural tourism, should be coordinated across administrations and maintained regardless of the electoral cycle.

Rural Spain does not need nostalgia; it needs opportunities.

Yours faithfully,

Elena Sanz
Zaragoza

tareas.titulo_es: Correo a un amigo sobre la preparación de la oposición
tareas.enunciado: An English friend, Tom, has written to ask how your preparation for the civil service exam is going and whether you would like to visit him in the summer. Write an email answering his questions, describing your daily routine and replying to his invitation.
estructura: Saludo informal y agradecimiento por su correo
Cómo va la preparación y tu rutina diaria
Respuesta a la invitación, con una pregunta práctica
Despedida informal
expresiones: Thanks so much for your email,
it was great to hear from you
which is a bit stressful but very useful
tareas.modelo:
Hi Tom,

Thanks so much for your email, it was great to hear from you!

The preparation is going well, although it's hard work. I usually start studying at eight in the morning and stop at about seven, with a long break for lunch and a walk. Twice a week I meet my tutor and present a topic out loud, which is a bit stressful but very useful. I'm also reading English newspapers every day to improve my vocabulary.

I'd love to visit you in the summer! The exam should be over by the end of June, so July would be perfect for me. Could you let me know which weeks suit you best? Then I'll start looking for flights.

Say hello to your family.

Speak soon,
Marta

tareas.titulo_es: Correo para pedir información sobre un curso de inglés
tareas.enunciado: You would like to take an intensive English course in Dublin next summer. Write an email to the language school asking about the dates and timetable, the price, accommodation with a host family and the level test.
estructura: Saludo y motivo del correo
Preguntas sobre fechas, horario y precio
Pregunta sobre el alojamiento
Pregunta sobre la prueba de nivel, indicando tu nivel
Agradecimiento y despedida
expresiones: I would like some more information
I would also like to know whether…
Thank you in advance for your help.
I look forward to hearing from you.
tareas.modelo:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am interested in taking an intensive English course at your school next summer and I would like some more information.

First, could you tell me the dates of the courses in July and August, and how many hours of classes there are per week? I would also like to know the total price and whether it includes course materials.

Secondly, I would prefer to stay with a host family. Is this possible, and how much does it cost per week?

Finally, I understand that students take a level test before the course. Is it done online before arrival or on the first day? My current level is about B2.

Thank you in advance for your help. I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Pablo Gómez

tareas.titulo_es: Correo a una Oficina Económica y Comercial para empezar a exportar
tareas.enunciado: You work for a small Spanish company that produces organic olive oil and wants to start exporting to Canada. Write an email to the Economic and Commercial Office of Spain in Toronto introducing your company and asking for information and support.
estructura: Asunto claro y saludo formal
Presentación de la empresa y del proyecto de exportación
Peticiones concretas, ordenadas (normativa, canales de distribución, ferias)
Pregunta sobre servicios personalizados y su coste
Ofrecimiento de más información, agradecimiento y firma con cargo
expresiones: I am writing on behalf of…
we are now considering… as our next export market
we would be grateful for your assistance with…
We would also like to know whether…
I would be happy to provide any further information
Thank you in advance for your help.
tareas.modelo:
Subject: Request for information on exporting organic olive oil to Canada

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing on behalf of Olivares del Sur, a family-owned company based in Jaén that has produced certified organic extra virgin olive oil for more than twenty years. We currently sell our products in Spain, France and Germany, and we are now considering Canada as our next export market.

Before taking a decision, we would be grateful for your assistance with the following points:
1) the labelling and certification requirements for organic food products in Canada;
2) the main distribution channels for high-quality olive oil, and whether it is more usual to work with importers or directly with retailers;
3) any trade fairs or promotional events in the coming year where we could meet potential buyers.

We would also like to know whether your office offers personalised services, such as market studies or the organisation of business meetings, and what they would cost.

I would be happy to provide any further information about our company. Thank you in advance for your help.

Yours faithfully,

Carmen López
Export Manager, Olivares del Sur

tareas.titulo_es: Correo a un cliente para comunicar el retraso de un pedido
tareas.enunciado: You are the sales manager of a Spanish manufacturer of industrial components. Because of a problem with a supplier, an important order for a British client will be delivered three weeks late. Write an email to the client informing them of the delay, explaining the reasons, apologising and proposing solutions to limit the impact.
estructura: Asunto y primera frase que comunique la mala noticia sin rodeos
Causa del retraso y medidas ya tomadas; nueva fecha
Disculpa y reconocimiento del perjuicio para el cliente
Propuestas concretas para compensar o limitar el impacto
Petición de respuesta, compromiso de seguimiento y firma
expresiones: I am writing to inform you that, regrettably,…
We have already secured an alternative source
As a result, we now expect to…
Please accept my sincere apologies for the inconvenience
We are fully aware of how important… is
With this in mind, we would like to propose…
I would be grateful if you could let me know whether this suits you
I will, of course, keep you informed
tareas.modelo:
Subject: Order 2417 – revised delivery date

Dear Mr Davies,

I am writing to inform you that, regrettably, we will not be able to deliver order 2417 on the agreed date of 14 May.

Last week a fire at the plant of one of our main suppliers of steel alloy interrupted deliveries to several manufacturers, including ourselves. We have already secured an alternative source, but the new material will not reach our factory until the end of this month. As a result, we now expect to ship your order on 4 June, three weeks later than planned.

Please accept my sincere apologies for the inconvenience this may cause to your production schedule. We are fully aware of how important this order is for you, and we would like to do everything possible to limit its impact. With this in mind, we would like to propose the following:
– a partial shipment, by air and at our expense, of the 40 % of the components that are already finished;
– a 5 % discount on the total value of the order.

I would be grateful if you could let me know whether this proposal suits you, or whether another arrangement would be more helpful. I will, of course, keep you informed of any progress.

Kind regards,

Andrés Morales
Sales Manager

tareas.titulo_es: Réplica a una tribuna: «Compra local, salva empleos»
tareas.enunciado: You have read an opinion piece in a local newspaper entitled «Buy local, save jobs». The author argues that imports from low-wage countries are destroying jobs in our factories and that the government should raise tariffs on these products. He adds that consumers have a duty to buy only national products, and concludes that free trade only benefits large multinational companies. Write a reply to be published in the same newspaper explaining why you disagree.
estructura: Título y referencia a la tribuna, resumiendo su tesis en una frase
Concesión inicial (compartes la preocupación) y anuncio del desacuerdo
Dos o tres contraargumentos ordenados (quién paga los aranceles, insumos importados y represalias, pymes exportadoras)
Matiz: qué hacer con los perdedores de la globalización
Conclusión breve
expresiones: In his article…, the author argues that…
Although I share his concern for…, I believe his conclusions are mistaken
are not paid by… but by…
Finally, it is not true that…
tareas.modelo:
Free trade is not the enemy

In his article «Buy local, save jobs», the author argues that imports from low-wage countries are destroying our industry and that higher tariffs would protect workers. Although I share his concern for those who have lost their jobs, I believe his conclusions are mistaken.

First of all, tariffs are not paid by foreign countries but by domestic consumers and businesses. Higher prices for imported goods reduce the purchasing power of families, especially those on lower incomes, who benefit most from affordable clothing, electronics and household appliances.

Secondly, many of our own companies depend on imported components to manufacture their products. Making these inputs more expensive would reduce their competitiveness and could therefore cost more jobs than it saves. We should also remember that other countries would probably respond with tariffs of their own, hitting our exporters.

Finally, it is not true that free trade only benefits large multinationals. Thousands of small and medium-sized Spanish firms sell their products abroad, from food to machinery, and they need open markets to grow.

This does not mean that the losers of globalisation should be ignored. However, the answer lies in training, support for the regions affected and fair competition rules, not in closing our borders.

tareas.titulo_es: Réplica a una tribuna: «El euro fue un error para el sur de Europa»
tareas.enunciado: An economist has published an opinion piece arguing that the euro has been a mistake for southern European countries. In his view, by giving up their own currencies these countries lost the ability to devalue in order to regain competitiveness, and the single monetary policy is designed for the needs of Germany. He concludes that the debt crisis of the 2010s proves that a monetary union cannot work without a full fiscal union, which will never exist. Write a reply for the same publication challenging his arguments.
estructura: Título y resumen de la tesis del autor; anuncio de tu desacuerdo
Rebatir el argumento de la devaluación (costes históricos, productividad)
Rebatir que la política monetaria esté hecha para Alemania
Conceder lo que tiene de cierto (fallos de diseño) y mostrar cómo ha respondido la UE
Conclusión: completar el euro, no deshacerlo
expresiones: In his recent column, the author claims that…
While his analysis raises real issues, his conclusion does not withstand scrutiny
The author is right, however, that…
The challenge, therefore, is not to… but to…
tareas.modelo:
The euro: imperfect, but not a mistake

In his recent column, the author claims that the euro has been a mistake for southern Europe, arguing that these countries lost the devaluation tool, that monetary policy serves German interests and that the debt crisis proved the project unworkable. While his analysis raises real issues, his conclusion does not withstand scrutiny.

To begin with, nostalgia for devaluation overlooks its costs. Before the euro, recurrent devaluations in Spain or Italy brought only temporary relief: they fuelled inflation, eroded real wages and kept interest rates high, because investors demanded a premium against the risk of further depreciation. Lasting competitiveness depends on productivity, not on the exchange rate.

Nor is it accurate to describe the single monetary policy as tailored to Germany. The European Central Bank sets its policy for the euro area as a whole, and many of its decisions over the last decade, from large-scale asset purchases to instruments designed to counter unwarranted divergences in sovereign spreads, were hardly what German public opinion favoured.

The author is right, however, that the debt crisis revealed serious flaws in the original design. Yet the Union has responded: the banking union, the European Stability Mechanism and the joint borrowing that financed the post-pandemic recovery would have been unthinkable twenty years ago. Integration has advanced, admittedly by trial and error, rather than collapsed.

The challenge, therefore, is not to undo the euro but to complete it, notably by finishing the banking union and building a common fiscal capacity.

tareas.titulo_es: Réplica a una tribuna sobre el salario mínimo
tareas.enunciado: A business association has published an op-ed claiming that recent increases in the minimum wage are a serious threat to employment. The authors argue that small businesses cannot afford higher labour costs and that the measure will push young and low-skilled workers out of the labour market or into the informal economy. They conclude that wages should be determined by productivity, not by government decree. Write a reply for the same newspaper, engaging critically with their arguments.
estructura: Título y resumen de la tribuna; reconocer la intención y anunciar la crítica (modelo teórico frente a evidencia)
Rebatir el supuesto de mercados perfectamente competitivos (poder de mercado del empleador) y citar la evidencia empírica sin inventar cifras
Concesión: límites de las subidas y propuesta de cómo fijarlo (comisión de expertos, evaluación, gradualidad)
Rebatir el argumento de la productividad (relación inversa salarios-productividad)
Responder a la economía sumergida y a las pymes con alternativas; conclusión
expresiones: Their concern for… is commendable; their reasoning, however, rests on…
This is not to say that…
As for the claim that…, it overlooks the fact that…
tareas.modelo:
The minimum wage: a question of evidence, not dogma

In their recent op-ed, the representatives of a business association warn that raising the minimum wage will price young and low-skilled workers out of the labour market, overwhelm small businesses and push employment into the informal economy. Their concern for the most vulnerable workers is commendable; their reasoning, however, rests on a textbook model that the empirical evidence of recent decades has called into question.

The claim that a wage floor necessarily destroys jobs assumes perfectly competitive labour markets, in which employers have no power to set wages. In reality, many low-wage workers face employers with considerable bargaining power, either because there are few alternatives locally or because changing jobs is costly. In such circumstances, a moderate minimum wage can raise pay without reducing employment, and may even draw more people into work. This is not wishful thinking: a large body of research, which began with studies of fast-food restaurants in the United States and has since been extended to many countries, has found small or negligible employment effects for moderate increases.

This is not to say that the minimum wage can be raised indefinitely with impunity. Beyond a certain level relative to the median wage, the risks the authors describe become real, particularly in regions where productivity is lower. A sensible policy should therefore rely on independent expert advice, regular evaluation and gradual adjustments, rather than on political announcements.

As for the claim that wages should be determined by productivity alone, it overlooks the fact that productivity itself depends partly on wages. Better pay reduces staff turnover, encourages training and pushes firms to invest in more efficient processes; low labour costs, conversely, can become a trap that delays modernisation.

Finally, the threat of informality calls for stronger labour inspection, not for lower wages, and small businesses in genuine difficulty would be better served by targeted measures, such as easier access to credit, than by a race to the bottom.

The debate deserves rigour on both sides. Rather than predicting catastrophe, let us assess each increase in the light of the data.

tareas.titulo_es: Informe: elección de un nuevo mercado de exportación
tareas.enunciado: Your company, a Spanish manufacturer of ceramic tiles, is considering entering a new foreign market. Your manager has asked you to write a short report comparing two possible markets of your choice, presenting the advantages and risks of each and making a recommendation.
estructura: Título e introducción: objetivo del informe
Primer mercado: ventajas e inconvenientes (con subtítulo)
Segundo mercado: ventajas e inconvenientes (con subtítulo)
Recomendación razonada y próximos pasos
expresiones: The aim of this report is to…
On balance, I recommend that we…
tareas.modelo:
Choosing a new export market

Introduction
The aim of this report is to compare the United Kingdom and Australia as possible new markets for our ceramic tiles and to recommend which one we should prioritise next year.

United Kingdom
The main advantage of the United Kingdom is its proximity, which keeps transport costs and delivery times low. Spanish tiles already enjoy a good reputation there, and the home renovation market is large and stable. However, competition is intense, and since the country left the European Union, exporters have faced additional customs formalities and new product marking requirements.

Australia
Australia offers a growing construction sector and strong demand for high-quality design products. Competition from European brands is also weaker than in the United Kingdom. On the other hand, the distance means higher transport costs and longer delivery times, and we have no existing contacts in the market.

Recommendation
On balance, I recommend that we focus first on the United Kingdom, where we can build on the reputation of Spanish tiles and test our products with a lower initial investment. Before taking a final decision, it would be advisable to contact the Spanish Economic and Commercial Office in London and to take part in a specialised trade fair to meet potential distributors. Australia could be considered at a later stage.

tareas.titulo_es: Informe sobre la participación en una feria comercial
tareas.enunciado: You have just attended an international food trade fair on behalf of your company. Write a report for your manager describing the event, the contacts you made and what you learnt about your competitors, and make recommendations for next year.
estructura: Título e introducción
El evento: asistencia y funcionamiento del estand
Contactos obtenidos y seguimiento previsto
Lo aprendido de los competidores
Recomendaciones y conclusión
expresiones: Five of them have already asked for…
For next year, I would recommend…
tareas.modelo:
Report on our participation in the international food fair

Introduction
This report summarises our participation in the international food fair held last week and makes recommendations for future editions.

The event
The fair was very well attended, with exhibitors from more than fifty countries. Our stand, in the Spanish pavilion, received a steady flow of visitors, particularly on the first two days, which were reserved for professionals.

Contacts
We met around thirty potential buyers, mainly importers and supermarket chains from northern Europe and the Middle East. Five of them have already asked for samples and price lists, and two have proposed a follow-up meeting next month.

Competitors
Italian and Greek producers had larger and more attractive stands, and several of them offered tastings, which clearly attracted more visitors. Many competitors also presented products in smaller, more modern packaging designed for single-person households.

Recommendations
For next year, I would recommend:
– booking a larger stand and organising tastings at fixed times;
– developing a range of smaller formats;
– preparing promotional material in English and Arabic;
– following up all contacts within two weeks of the fair.

Conclusion
Overall, the fair was a worthwhile investment, and it could lead to new export opportunities if we act quickly.

tareas.titulo_es: Informe de evaluación del teletrabajo híbrido
tareas.enunciado: A year ago your organisation introduced a hybrid working scheme (three days in the office and two at home). Management has asked you to write a report assessing the scheme and making recommendations. Use the following information from a staff survey and internal indicators: 78 % of staff are satisfied with the scheme; sick leave has fallen by 15 %; productivity indicators are stable; new employees say they find it hard to learn from colleagues; meeting rooms are overbooked on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
estructura: Título y propósito del informe
Resultados positivos, integrando los datos del enunciado con conectores de causa y consecuencia
Puntos débiles detectados
Recomendaciones concretas (pasiva y estructuras formales: it is recommended that…)
Conclusión breve
expresiones: Overall, the scheme has been well received
This appears to have had a positive effect on…
has not come at the expense of…
In the light of these findings,
it is recommended that the scheme be maintained
a follow-up survey should be carried out
tareas.modelo:
Assessment of the hybrid working scheme

Purpose
This report evaluates the first year of the hybrid working scheme and puts forward recommendations for its future.

Main findings
Overall, the scheme has been well received: 78 % of employees are satisfied with it, citing in particular the time saved on commuting and a better work-life balance. This appears to have had a positive effect on well-being, as sick leave has fallen by 15 %. Importantly, productivity indicators have remained stable, which suggests that the scheme has not come at the expense of performance.

Nevertheless, two weaknesses have emerged. Firstly, new employees report that they find it difficult to learn from more experienced colleagues, since informal exchanges are less frequent. Secondly, the concentration of office days on Tuesdays and Wednesdays has led to a shortage of meeting rooms on those days, while the building remains underused on Mondays and Fridays.

Recommendations
In the light of these findings, it is recommended that the scheme be maintained, subject to the following adjustments:
– new staff should spend four days a week in the office during their first three months and be assigned a mentor;
– office days should be spread more evenly across the week through a team rota, which would ease the pressure on meeting rooms;
– a follow-up survey should be carried out in six months' time to assess the impact of these changes.

Conclusion
The scheme has delivered clear benefits at no apparent cost to productivity. With minor adjustments, it can also meet the needs of newcomers and make better use of office space.

tareas.titulo_es: Propuesta de un programa de apoyo a pymes que empiezan a exportar
tareas.enunciado: The regional government is inviting proposals to help small and medium-sized enterprises start exporting. Write a proposal describing a programme: the problem it addresses, its objective, its main actions and how its results would be measured.
estructura: Título del programa
Antecedentes: el problema y los obstáculos de las empresas
Objetivo cuantificado
Acciones principales, por fases
Evaluación con indicadores y conclusión
expresiones: The aim of this programme would be to…
The main obstacles they mention are…
The programme would consist of three stages
would cover half of the cost of…
tareas.modelo:
Proposal: «First Steps Abroad» programme for new exporters

Background
Many small and medium-sized enterprises in our region produce high-quality goods but have never sold abroad. The main obstacles they mention are a lack of information about foreign markets, limited language skills and the cost of the first trips to meet buyers.

Objective
The aim of this programme would be to help one hundred firms that have never exported to make their first sales in a foreign market within two years.

Main actions
The programme would consist of three stages. First, each company would receive a free diagnosis of its export potential, carried out by a specialist consultant. Secondly, participants would attend practical training in areas such as international contracts, payment methods and digital marketing. Finally, the regional government would cover half of the cost of taking part in a trade fair or a trade mission, in coordination with the national export promotion agency.

Evaluation
Results would be measured using simple indicators: the number of companies that make a first export sale, the value of these sales and the number of firms that are still exporting two years after the end of the programme.

Conclusion
With a moderate budget, this programme could broaden our export base and make the regional economy more resilient.

tareas.titulo_es: Propuesta para reducir el tráfico en el centro de la ciudad
tareas.enunciado: Your city council has launched a public consultation on how to reduce traffic and pollution in the city centre. On behalf of a residents' association, write a proposal setting out the current situation, two or three concrete measures, their expected benefits and how possible objections could be addressed.
estructura: Título y situación actual
Medidas propuestas, ordenadas y concretas
Beneficios esperados
Respuesta anticipada a las objeciones (comercio, residentes) y mecanismo de seguimiento
Fórmula de cierre dirigida al ayuntamiento
expresiones: On behalf of…, we would like to put forward…
Firstly, we propose the creation of…
the council should improve alternatives to the car
Experience in other European cities suggests that…
We trust that the council will give this proposal careful consideration.
tareas.modelo:
Proposal for a cleaner and more liveable city centre

Current situation
The historic centre suffers from heavy congestion throughout the day. Residents complain of noise and poor air quality, pedestrians and cyclists share narrow streets with cars and delivery vans, and local shops are worried about falling visitor numbers.

Proposed measures
On behalf of the residents' association, we would like to put forward three measures. Firstly, we propose a low-emission zone covering the historic centre, with access restricted to residents, public transport, emergency services and clean vehicles. Secondly, deliveries should be concentrated in early-morning time slots and, wherever possible, made by electric vans or cargo bikes from a logistics hub on the outskirts. Thirdly, the council should improve alternatives to the car by increasing bus frequency, creating protected cycle lanes and building park-and-ride facilities at the main entrances to the city.

Expected benefits
These measures would reduce pollution and noise, improve road safety and make the centre more attractive for walking and shopping. Experience in other European cities suggests that, once the initial adjustment period is over, pedestrianised areas tend to attract more customers, not fewer.

Addressing objections
We are aware that some shopkeepers fear losing customers and that some residents depend on their cars. For this reason, we recommend introducing the measures gradually, with an information campaign and exemptions for people with reduced mobility. A monitoring committee including traders and residents could evaluate the results after the first year.

We trust that the council will give this proposal careful consideration.

tareas.titulo_es: Reseña de una aplicación para aprender idiomas
tareas.enunciado: An English-language website for students is asking readers to review a language-learning app they have used. Write a review describing the app, saying what you liked and didn't like, and explaining whether you would recommend it and to whom.
estructura: Título que resuma tu valoración
Presentación: cuánto tiempo la has usado y para qué
Descripción y aspectos positivos
Aspectos negativos
Recomendación final: a quién sí y a quién no
expresiones: so I think I can give an honest opinion
However, the app also has some weak points
I would recommend… to anyone who…
But if you need…, you will have to…
tareas.modelo:
WordWise: good for vocabulary, not enough for speaking

I have been using WordWise for three months to prepare for my English exam, so I think I can give an honest opinion.

The app is free, although some extra features cost a few euros a month. Every day it gives you short exercises of about ten minutes: new words, listening activities and small grammar tests. I really like the design, which is clear and colourful, and the way it reminds you of words you have forgotten. Thanks to it, my vocabulary has improved a lot.

However, the app also has some weak points. The speaking exercises are very limited: you only repeat sentences and you never have a real conversation. Also, the grammar explanations are sometimes too short for difficult topics.

All in all, I would recommend WordWise to anyone who wants to learn new words in a fun way, especially on the bus or during short breaks. But if you need to improve your speaking, you will have to find a teacher or a conversation partner too.

tareas.titulo_es: Reseña de un ensayo económico
tareas.enunciado: A cultural magazine has asked its readers to review a book on economics or society that has influenced their thinking. Write a review summarising the book's main argument, assessing its strengths and weaknesses, and saying who would benefit from reading it.
estructura: Título y presentación del libro (autor, obra, por qué importa)
Tesis central resumida con tus palabras
Puntos fuertes
Puntos débiles o críticas recibidas
Recomendación: a qué lector se dirige
expresiones: Few… have reached as wide an audience as…
The central argument is deceptively simple
The book's greatest strength lies in…
The work is not without weaknesses, however
tareas.modelo:
A book that put inequality back at the centre of economics

Few economics books have reached as wide an audience as Thomas Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century. More than a decade after its publication in English, it remains an essential reference for anyone interested in the distribution of wealth.

Piketty's central argument is deceptively simple. Drawing on tax records covering more than two centuries in several countries, he shows that the relatively equal societies of the decades after the Second World War were an exception, made possible by wars, inflation and progressive taxation. When the return on capital exceeds the growth rate of the economy, which he summarises in the famous inequality r > g, inherited wealth tends to grow faster than income from work, and fortunes become increasingly concentrated.

The book's greatest strength lies in its data. By constructing long historical series, Piketty shifted the debate on inequality from abstract theory to empirical evidence, and he did so in a clear and often elegant style, enlivened by references to the novels of Balzac and Jane Austen.

The work is not without weaknesses, however. Several economists have argued that much of the rise in the capital share is explained by housing rather than by the mechanism he describes. Moreover, his main policy proposal, a global progressive tax on wealth, seems difficult to implement in a world of tax competition, as the author himself acknowledges.

Despite its length, the book is accessible to non-specialists willing to devote time to it. I would recommend it to students of economics and to anyone seeking to understand why inequality has become one of the defining issues of our time.

tareas.titulo_es: Nota a los compañeros sobre un traslado de oficina
tareas.enunciado: Your department is moving to a different floor of the building next week. Write a note to your colleagues explaining when the move will take place, what they need to do before then and whom to contact if they have any questions.
estructura: Título o encabezado y saludo
Qué va a pasar y cuándo
Lo que deben hacer antes (lista breve con verbos en imperativo)
A quién dirigirse y agradecimiento
expresiones: The move will take place on…
If you have any questions, please contact…
tareas.modelo:
Office move next week

Dear colleagues,

As you know, our department is moving from the second to the fifth floor. The move will take place on Friday 12 April, so the office will be closed that day and everyone should work from home.

Before you leave on Thursday, please:
– put your personal belongings and documents in the boxes provided;
– write your name on each box;
– switch off and unplug your computer.

The new office will be ready on Monday morning. If you have any questions, please contact Ana in the administration team (extension 245).

Thank you for your cooperation.

Luis

tareas.titulo_es: Nota interna sobre el nuevo procedimiento de gastos de viaje
tareas.enunciado: As head of administration, you must inform staff about changes to the procedure for claiming travel expenses, which will come into force next month. Write an internal memo explaining the main changes, the reasons for them and where staff can get help.
estructura: Encabezado de memorando (To / From / Subject)
Anuncio del cambio y fecha de entrada en vigor
Principales cambios en una lista breve
Motivos de los cambios
Formación o contacto para dudas y cierre
expresiones: The main changes are as follows:
tareas.modelo:
MEMO

To: All staff
From: Head of Administration
Subject: New procedure for travel expense claims

Please note that, as from 1 March, travel expenses will be claimed through the new online platform instead of on paper forms.

The main changes are as follows:
– claims must be submitted within thirty days of the end of the trip;
– a photograph or scan of each receipt must be uploaded with the claim, and original paper receipts will no longer be required;
– trips abroad will need prior approval from your head of department on the platform.

These changes are intended to speed up reimbursements, which should now be paid within two weeks, and to reduce the use of paper. They also bring our procedures into line with the recommendations of the latest internal audit.

A short training session will be held on 20 February at 10 a.m. in the main meeting room. In the meantime, if you have any questions, please contact the administration team.

Thank you for your cooperation.
